subject: Hosted evaluation: quickstart options, endpoints & rate caps (recap + next steps)
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@finlytics.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 16:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intro / Hosted eval next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap from our side and a few questions so we can decide whether to proceed with a Hosted pilot or look at Dedicated capacity.

Summary of what we need (high-level):
- Real-time customer-facing assistant (avg response target < 250ms p95) for support use cases.
- Peak: ~400 reqs/min during business hours; baseline ~60 reqs/min. Many short prompts (100-200 tokens).
- Data residency: US only; standard SOC2 is fine for now but procurement will ask about audit logs.

Questions:
1) For the Hosted API, what endpoint types would you recommend for low-latency (single-tenant endpoints vs shared)?
2) What are the realistic rate caps and burst behavior for a hosted pilot? Can we expect graceful throttling or queued requests?
3) If we outgrow Hosted, what does the migration path to Dedicated look like (lead time, config migration)?

If useful, I can share a short CSV with our hourly traffic profile. Procurement also wants a ballpark on monthly token cost for the pilot (≈1M tokens/day).

Thanks — if you can reply with a quick checklist/next-steps we can review internally and get procurement aligned.

— Elena
Elena Park
Head of Product, Finlytics
elena.park@finlytics.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finlytics.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intro / Hosted eval next steps

Elena — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front, then a suggested quickstart checklist and proposed next steps.

Quick answers:
- Endpoint types: start on a shared Hosted endpoint with a provisioned sandbox that has dedicated concurrency slices (gives lowest friction). If p95 < 250ms becomes strict, we recommend moving to a per-customer single-tenant endpoint (Hosted dedicated endpoint) — we can provision this without full Dedicated capacity in many cases.
- Rate caps & bursts: default hosted plan enforces per-endpoint rate caps; for pilots we can set a temporary elevated cap (e.g., 600 reqs/min) for 2 weeks while we validate. Throttling is graceful — token-level queuing up to a buffer, then 429s if sustained.
- Migration path: config (model + prompt templates + KV prefix cache keys) is exported; moving to Dedicated is typically a 2–4 week operational window depending on capacity and region.

Attached is a short hosted quickstart checklist for the pilot (attachment: hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf). Key asks from our side:
- Finalize traffic profile (hourly CSV) — helps us pre-configure autoscale and batching.
- Confirm target latency SLO and any hard block (e.g., must be <150ms).
- Security contact for SOC2/audit data retention questions so we can surface the right artifacts.

Suggested next steps:
1) Elena: share traffic_profile.csv (we can treat as draft).
2) We: provision sandbox endpoints + elevated rate cap for 14 days; share sandbox endpoint URL and credentials.
3) Quick technical call (30 min) to finalize latency SLO and KV cache strategy.
4) Procurement: we’ll send a pilot quote (monthly estimate) and SOC2 packet.

If you want, I can copy in Sean to coordinate procurement and pricing.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finlytics.com>, markus.klein@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intro / Hosted eval next steps

Elena — quick technical clarifications from my side (so we size the endpoints correctly):

- Latency: p95 depends on prompt length and model selection. For short prompts (≤200 tokens) with an optimized gpt-like open model we commonly hit ~160–220ms p95 on hosted slices. If you need <150ms p95 consistently, we should plan for a single-tenant hosted endpoint or Dedicated.
- Concurrency & batching: at 400 reqs/min peak, concurrency patterns matter. Please indicate whether bursts are spread across many users (good for batching) or concentrated in a few sessions (less batching benefit).
- Caching: prefix/KV cache is effective for support templates; if you have many repeated opening lines we can reduce cost by >30%.

Operational notes:
- For the pilot, we recommend these sandbox settings: 2x concurrency slices, burst cap 800 reqs/min, token buffer 10k tokens queued. We’ll monitor and adjust.
- Security: if procurement asks for audit logs, we can provide token-level latency traces and retained request metadata for 90 days (default). For longer retention or custom retention policies we’ll loop in Security.

I’ll stand up a short tech session once you share the CSV.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, procurement@finlytics.com

Subject: Re: Intro / Hosted eval next steps

Thanks Markus and Jordan — this is perfect. Attaching a simplified hourly traffic_profile.csv (attachment: traffic_profile.csv). Procurement looped on this thread; they asked for the SOC2 packet and a rough pilot cost estimate (monthly).

Decision: Finlytics would like to try a 2-week Hosted pilot with the elevated rate cap you suggested. Goals for the pilot:
- Validate p95 latency under our real traffic (<250ms target)
- Confirm cost run-rate at ~1M tokens/day
- Evaluate prefix caching benefits for our templated responses

Next actions from our side:
- Procurement: review pilot quote when you send it.
- Elena: share any security contact details if you need SOC2 questions answered.

Please proceed with sandbox provisioning and I’ll book the tech session for Thursday morning.

— Elena
